notable_anecdotes: The Agrava Board's extraordinary scale: 125 sessions, 194 witnesses, 20,377 pages of transcript -- and still no definitive mastermind.
Justice Corazon Agrava's lone dissent from the 4-1 Board conclusion pointing to Gen. Ver.
Andres Narvasa serving as Agrava Board general counsel before rising to Chief Justice -- a biographical detail showing the era's institutional connections.
Ver's flight to Hawaii with Marcos on February 25, 1986 (the day of EDSA) stripping the SBN of jurisdiction over him -- he died in Bangkok on November 21, 1998, never convicted.

Former Ambassador Bienvenido Tan Jr.'s private letter to the author dated March 15, 2009 -- as the Agrava Board's own public coordinator, Tan attested that there was 'never any evidence linking President Marcos or Imelda or Danding.'
The 2004 PAO motion for a new trial (Persida Acosta) based on forensic evidence suggesting the fatal shot came not from Moreno (behind Ninoy on the stairway) but from Rolando Galman (on the tarmac).

one_paragraph_summary: On the 35th anniversary of Ninoy Aquino's August 21, 1983 assassination at the MIA tarmac, Panganiban traces the legal proceedings that identified the soldiers but left the mastermind an enduring enigma. President Marcos first created a fact-finding committee chaired by CJ Enrique Fernando (August 24, 1983), then replaced it on October 22, 1983 with the Agrava Board (chair: Justice Corazon Agrava; assisted by 'Gray Dean' Andres Narvasa as general counsel) -- which held 125 sessions, heard 194 witnesses, and produced 20,377 pages of transcript before concluding 4-1 (Agrava dissented) that Gen. Fabian Ver and several military officers conspired to kill Ninoy. The SBN Pamaran decision of December 2, 1985 acquitted all accused; the newly reconstituted post-EDSA Supreme Court found it 'to be a sham,' nullified it, and ordered a new trial. In the Hermosisima decision of September 28, 1990, the SBN convicted the soldiers and sentenced them to reclusion perpetua, identifying CIC Rogelio Moreno as the triggerman behind Ninoy on the stairway -- though a 2004 PAO motion for a new trial (Persida Acosta) argued forensic evidence pointed instead to Rolando Galman on the tarmac. Ver was charged with murder but never tried: he fled to Hawaii with Marcos on February 25, 1986, died in Bangkok on November 21, 1998, and was never convicted as coconspirator or mastermind. Loose talk linking Marcos, Imelda, and Danding Cojuangco was never substantiated -- the Agrava Board's own public coordinator, former Ambassador Bienvenido Tan Jr., wrote the author on March 15, 2009, that 'there was never any evidence linking President Marcos or Imelda or Danding so that much as we might have wanted... we could not in good conscience come up with that conclusion.' After 35 years and two Aquino presidencies, Panganiban concludes, the identity of the mastermind remains a legal enigma.
